(P1) Error grows monotonically with wind rotation: M1 x1.84 / x2.59 / x3.74 and M2 x1.96 / x2.95 / x4.57 of nominal at 5 / 10 / 20 degrees with 4 sensors; with 9 sensors M1 x2.72 / x4.51 / x7.33 and M2 x2.77 / x4.58 / x7.46. (P2) M2's advantage over the fair M1 at 4 sensors erodes with misspecification: -20% nominal, -15% / -9% / -3% at 5 / 10 / 20 degrees, -7% combined; M2's ratio degradation is slightly larger than M1's (x4.57 vs x3.74 at 20 degrees) but in absolute terms M2 error is lower than M1's in every one of the 20 layout x condition cells; TV does not buy robustness. Other effects: speed error x0.8 / x1.2 costs x2.07 / x1.68 (4 sensors, M1) and x2.17 / x2.06 (9 sensors); diffusion x2 costs x1.80 (M1, 4 sensors) / x3.40 (9 sensors); an unmodelled constant source of 10% / 30% of the mean local emission costs x1.04 / x1.37 (4 sensors) and x2.00 / x4.58 (9 sensors). Using history helps a lot: the causal filter lowers sqrt(J_pop) relative to the current-time-only estimator by 56% / 52% (4 sensors, 2% / 10% noise; -0.00695 [-0.00910,-0.00482] and -0.00652 [-0.00865,-0.00449] ug/m3) and 80% / 77% (9 sensors); retrospective smoothing (which also uses FUTURE data) improves on the causal filter by a further 55% / 58% (4 sensors) and 32% / 36% (9 sensors) (-0.00305 [-0.00446,-0.00194], -0.00346 [-0.00483,-0.00237], -0.00061 [-0.00087,-0.00041], -0.00079 [-0.00104,-0.00059]); the full-history independent-bin M1 beats the causal filter by 43% / 45% (4 sensors) and 31% / 35% (9 sensors). All 12 primary contrasts meet the registered criterion (CI excludes 0 at Bonferroni 0.05/4, >=10% relative gain, sign persists leaving each wind out). Change detection (episodes with a step in an identifiable parameter, n=58; detected when the estimate crosses halfway between the pre- and post-levels): CT misses 41-55% of changes; the causal filter misses 2-5% and, at 4 sensors, detects with a mean delay of 0.48 bins (about 29 min on 1 h bins) vs 0.32 for the smoother (the smoother's advantage is partly hindsight). Median mesh-induced displacement (500 m | 2 km | replicate pairs): 2108 | 2262 | 3691 m (budget 3, 0.05); 2738 | 2567 | 3147 m (5, 0.05); 1118 | 2370 | 3996 m (3, 0.15); 1728 | 3234 | 3468 m (5, 0.15). Median |regret| (reference-objective units): control 6.8e-6..4.4e-5, replicate pairs 2.6e-5, 6.0e-5, 6.3e-5, 1.9e-4 (control medians are 10-25% of the pair medians, not zero). Layouts from 6-case ensembles move by 3-4 km between independent draws, more than degrading the mesh spacing 2x (500 m) or 8x (2 km), so mesh effects are invisible through design noise. This does not show 500 m is adequate (it stays provisionally admissible only) and is consistent with, but not a demonstration about, F-035 (which argued analytically that a different, unpaired test could not fail). COST CORRECTION: a version with 48 or 96 cases per draw costs 8x or 16x this run per draw count, i.e. ~190 or ~375 core-hours for 8 draws (about 94 or 188 for 4 draws) at the observed efficiency; the suggestion that 48-96 cases suffice extrapolates the toy DYN-05 result (ridge risk, 70 cells, k=2,3) to Belauri greedy_total and is a guess. Caveats: padded domain differs from the unpadded one; the 2 km control needed a control-only origin-tag relaxation (D-016; labels only, the total objective does not use tags); budgets 3 and 5 are not independent tests.
